summary: Cold Q4 found bidirectional misalignment: the verifier forces idle confirmation onto the replica alias despite runbook “may use” language, couples /readyz pins-unreachable to a monkeypatched helper name, never asserts the stated django_session pin prohibition, and never requires dump accepting_checkout to become true under a healthy conjunction. Instruction shape and delegated runbook/oncall/ha.json boundary are otherwise sound.

evidence.observation: Two-paragraph work request: preserve manage.py and checkout/health/ready routes; fenced-writer writes; no lagged sticky reads; sticky keys must not live in django_session; one capture per attempt_id; reject empty attempt_id; refuse pay/capture when order write_lsn ahead of writer wal_lsn; /readyz 503 for double-writable, seq gap past max_lag_lsn, old writer still allowed, pins unreachable, or repeat captures; write /app/ha/out/failover-status.json per runbook object. References oncall, error log, shop files, pins alias, and /app/ha/docs/runbook.md.

Operator commands sync_standby/cutover/dump_failover; fence lease (owner_node, epoch); sticky via pins key sticky:shopper:<id> not django_session; lag gate primary.wal_lsn-replica.applied_lsn<=max_lag_lsn with wording “Other reads may use replica only when…”; live /readyz vs stricter dump accepting_checkout (pins==shared, standby_only_orders==0, incident orders on standby, fence_copied_to_standby false); exact failover-status.json field set.
Incident notes support instruction current-state claims (AZ-B writer, replica POST place, OPEN confirmation, dual captures, writable lease on standby) without prescribing repair modules.
Captured gunicorn/error lines corroborate replica inserts, sticky miss on django_session, dual captures for att-inc-*, sync cutoff, writable lease copy, and /readyz equated to /healthz.
Public knobs sticky_seconds=5, max_lag_lsn=25, incident_min_order_id=19980, nodes az-a/az-b, resource checkout-primary.

Enumerated F2P/P2P suite covering writer placement, AZ-B standby growth, sticky via confirmation alias and pins cache, sync/cutover/epoch/lease, capture idempotency, write_lsn gate, /readyz failure modes (including monkeypatch of controlplane.desk_state.pins_reachable), dump schema keys and negative accepting_checkout cases, plus preservation of manage.py/routes/schema/blank attempt. No assert of accepting_checkout True; no assert that ShopSession lacks sticky keys; idle-read test requires alias==replica after sync; final P2P lag assert is vacuous (or True).

pins_reachable() probes pin-cache and caches['pins']; collect_desk_snapshot feeds live vs dump readiness. Confirms the monkeypatched symbol is an internal helper, not a documented public operator contract.
Starter confirmation_payload includes alias/order_ref/status/write_lsn/primary_lsn; alias is an environment response field used by tests but not documented in instruction/runbook schemas.
Instruction must carry material requirements; docs may hold protocol/schema; every tested behavior must be discoverable; grading-relevant ambiguity and phantom tests are Q4 defects.

findings.criterion: phantom-spec / reverse-matrix: verifier behavior not discoverable as a MUST from solver-visible contract
findings.why_it_matters: Runbook permits replica use only when lag is in budget (“may use”); instruction only forbids serving a just-written shopper from a lagged standby. test_f2p_idle_read_follows_seq_gap requires confirmation body alias=="replica" after sync, rejecting an otherwise correct always-writer-or-sticky-default read path and changing pass/fail for conforming solutions.
findings.minimal_remediation: Weaken the post-sync assertion to lag eligibility / standby_readable / non-stale order semantics, or change runbook language to a mandatory idle-replica routing rule if that is truly required.
findings.regression_risk: Low if tests keep sticky-on-writer and high-lag unreable checks; do not drop seq-gap gating.

findings.criterion: req-gap / forward-matrix: material requirement not meaningfully tested
findings.why_it_matters: Instruction and runbook require sticky keys must not live in django_session on either shop file. Session-wipe and pins-get tests prove pins can work without relying solely on session, but never assert absence of sticky rows/keys in ShopSession/django_session after place. Dual-write-to-session implementations can still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: After place, assert no sticky:shopper:<id> (or equivalent) row remains in django_session/ShopSession on default and replica, while pins still holds the pin.
findings.regression_risk: Low; preserve existing pin survival and shared-pins checks.

findings.why_it_matters: Pins-unreachable → /readyz non-200 is a discoverable requirement, but the test only fails readiness by monkeypatching controlplane.desk_state.pins_reachable. Equivalent implementations that probe pins without calling that symbol keep pins actually reachable under the patch and can wrongly fail, so the graded contract is a private helper name rather than the observable store failure.
findings.minimal_remediation: Induce unreachable pins via the public store (e.g., break/remove pin-cache backend or override CACHES['pins'] to a failing backend) without patching a specific function symbol.
findings.regression_risk: Medium if readiness composition is refactored; keep other /readyz gates intact.

findings.why_it_matters: Runbook defines dump accepting_checkout as true only under a strict healthy conjunction (live gates plus pins==shared, no standby-only orders, incident orders on standby, fence not writable on standby). Every dump test only asserts accepting_checkout is False under injected faults. An always-false accepting_checkout implementation satisfies all of those assertions and never has to implement the positive conjunction, so the graded dump contract is incomplete.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a healed-lab case (single writable writer, gap in budget, shared reachable pins, no repeat captures, incident orders synced, no writable standby lease, no standby-only rows) that asserts accepting_checkout is True and pins=="shared".
findings.regression_risk: Medium fixture setup cost; keep existing negative dump cases.

findings.why_it_matters: Final assert `lag_lsn() <= budget or True` always passes and does not preserve or exercise the named seq-gap budget behavior.
findings.minimal_remediation: Replace with a real behavioral check of budgeted replica eligibility, or delete the vacuous assert.

findings.why_it_matters: Runbook/config require post-write sticky for sticky_seconds; tests check pin presence/survival but not TTL expiry. Non-blocking because sticky routing itself is graded elsewhere.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional TTL expiry metamorphic using config sticky_seconds; not required to clear F1–F4.
findings.regression_risk: Flaky if wall-clock sleeps are used; prefer controlled clock/TTL override.

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction lists “the old writer is still allowed” as a distinct /readyz 503 cause; live runbook gates phrase this as exactly one writable writer. Likely the same double-writable case already tested, so advisory unless authors intend a separate affinity gate.
findings.minimal_remediation: Align instruction wording with runbook live /readyz gates, or add an explicit distinct gate both documented and tested.

Pay/capture refuses when order write_lsn ahead of writer wal_lsn
/readyz 503 when both files writable / seq gap past max_lag_lsn / pins unreachable / repeat captures; distinct from /healthz liveness
Write /app/ha/out/failover-status.json with runbook object fields and dump accepting_checkout semantics
Fence lease epoch moves forward; demoted/standby lease not left writable; sync copies business/incident rows and watermarks
Non-sticky reads may use replica only when lag <= max_lag_lsn
